items.t: AI Agent Swarms Run Up “$1 Million” Bills Before Detection, Palo Alto’s Unit 42 Says
items.sum: Key TakeawaysPalo Alto’s Unit 42 found stolen AI keys running up nearly $1 million in charges before victims caught them. Companies can’t rely solely on AI labs for protection, creating an opening for security vendors.

items.t: CrowdStrike and Palo Alto Networks Climb 3% as Microsoft Outage Disrupts Outlook and Teams
items.sum: When Microsoft stumbles, some cybersecurity stocks catch a bid. But one leader is still sliding while its rival surges, and an earnings report next week could decide whether this rebound has legs or fades as fast as the outage.
